Graph-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Graph-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation addresses the limitations of large language models with long-context inputs and multi-hop queries by introducing explicit relational modeling.

LightRAG
LightRAG is a reference method for text-based knowledge graph construction, specifically designed as a graph-enhanced RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system that integrates structured knowledge representation with dual-level retrieval mechanisms. It is also a sparsified index approach within the GraphRAG framework, optimized for retrieval efficiency. LightRAG has demonstrated moderate performance, achieving 85.0% accuracy in the 'Multimodal' document type and 59.7% in the 'Text-only' domain. The method shows the best accuracy in 'Research Reports/Introductions' and the worst in 'Guidebooks'. LightRAG is primarily a text-only content processing framework, used in various case studies to answer questions, including those about visual documents and financial table navigation. However, it has also been noted to provide incorrect answers in visual analysis tasks, with one instance of an AI model from LightRAG giving an incorrect response.

MMGraphRAG is a multimodal retrieval framework that constructs unified knowledge graphs spanning textual and visual content, linking scene graphs with textual representations to integrate external knowledge from diverse data modalities. It has achieved 67.6% accuracy in the 'Multimodal' document type and 60.5% in the 'Text-only' domain, performing similarly to LightRAG. MMGraphRAG treats tables and equations as plain text and includes basic image processing. It is used in case studies to answer questions about visual documents, but has also been noted for providing incorrect answers in financial table navigation and visual analysis. RAG-Anything
RAG-Anything is a comprehensive framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that excels in multimodal knowledge unification and long-context document understanding. It is designed to address the limitations of existing text-centric systems by extending GraphRAG to all modalities, including visual elements, structured data, and mathematical expressions. RAG-Anything employs a dual-graph construction strategy, enhancing its performance on long documents through cross-modal hybrid retrieval. This framework demonstrates advanced visual reasoning and complex tabular data handling capabilities, making it a robust system for multimodal document understanding.

RAG-Anything is an all-in-one RAG framework that outperforms other methods in accuracy across various domains, particularly in information-dense contexts. It is noted for its superior performance on long documents compared to MM-GraphRAG and is used in case studies to answer questions about visual documents and financial table navigation. The system is designed to handle complex visual reasoning tasks and is used in the analysis and evaluation of multimodal document understanding. RAG-Anything is an advanced retrieval and augmentation framework that constructs modality-aware graphs to manage complex document layouts, and it has demonstrated systematic factual accuracy in various tasks.

GPT-4o-mini
GPT-4o-mini is a powerful multimodal language model with native text and image understanding capabilities. It is used in various experimental frameworks and case studies, including accuracy evaluations and comprehensive experimental consistency and reliability checks. GPT-4o-mini achieved 61.0% overall accuracy on the DocBench Dataset, performing particularly well in 'Tutorials/Workshops' and poorly in 'Academic Papers'. In some case studies, it provided incorrect answers, such as in financial table navigation and visual analysis. Despite these limitations, GPT-4o-mini is a key model used for answering questions about visual documents and comparing responses in experimental evaluations.

DocBench
DocBench is a multimodal benchmark dataset used to evaluate the performance of RAG-Anything and other retrieval and augmentation methods. Specifically, DocBench consists of 229 documents, each averaging 66 pages and 46,377 tokens, across five critical domains, with financial reports being the most extensive category. These documents are used to assess model performance on both long and shorter documents, as well as for ablation studies in the context of document reasoning tasks. The benchmark spans a range of document types and includes 1,102 questions, making it a comprehensive tool for evaluating document understanding systems. DocBench is particularly useful for evaluating the performance of multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, providing a robust framework for comparing different approaches in the field.

MMLongBench
MMLongBench is a multimodal benchmark dataset primarily used to evaluate the performance of models on long-context documents. It is designed to assess the effectiveness of methods in handling longer documents and is particularly relevant for long-document reasoning tasks. The dataset contains 135 documents, each averaging 47.5 pages and 21,214 tokens, across 7 document types, with 1,082 questions. These documents include a variety of types such as research reports, tutorials, and academic papers, which maintain moderate lengths. MMLongBench is utilized in multimodal document understanding tasks and is also relevant for validating the effectiveness of RAG-Anything, a specific multimodal benchmark.
